chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee' who said:
I asked Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) about prayer in Mecca and Medina: is it shortened (qasr) or complete (tamm)? He said, 'Shorten it as long as you do not intend to stay for ten days.'

key_terms.اَلرِّضَا: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him), the 8th Imam
key_terms.تَقْصِيرٌ: Shortening of prayers (performing 2 rak'ahs instead of 4)
key_terms.مُقَامِ عَشَرَةٍ: Intending to stay for ten days

ai.seo_question: When does a traveler need to shorten their prayers in Mecca and Medina according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the condition for shortening prayers (qasr) in the holy cities of Mecca and Medina, establishing that the traveler remains a traveler unless they intend to stay for ten days or more. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it aligns with the general principle of travel prayer, emphasizing that intention (niyyah) of a ten-day stay transforms the status from traveler to resident, thereby requiring full prayer. The hadith is cited in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* to resolve nuances regarding whether the sanctity of the city itself alters the standard rules of travel.
